children: Wall Street
the week in the red after a nearly 20-basis-point jump in the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield
and the latest consumer price index inflation report landing.
U.S. Treasury yields
across the curve this week, with the benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (

) climbing nearly 20 basis points to 4.97%. U.S. CPI inflation rose 0.4% M/M in August, matching Wall Street estimates and accelerating from July’s 0.1% gain, according to Friday’s Bureau of Labor Statistics data release.
State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF
was down 1.46% from the previous week to $57.25.
Among megacap stocks, Royal Bank of Canada
led the decliners, retreating 2.91% week-over-week to $205.90.
Mastercard
(-2.82% W/W to $569.19) and Visa
(-2.19% W/W to $370.45) were the other notable decliners.
The week saw Ant International, Mastercard
, and Visa
launch an initiative to establish standard identification and verification for AI agents executing purchases on behalf of users.
Wells Fargo
topped the gainers in the category, advancing 1.23% from the prior week to close at $90.29.
Crypto stocks Hut 8
(+11.93% W/W to $98.60) and IREN
(+5.23% W/W to $43.83) led the largecap gainers.
Circle Internet
(-12.23% W/W to $90.60) and Carlyle Group
(-11.33% W/W to $42.34) topped the losers in the category.
Blue Owl

retreated 10.81% to $10.56 amid fresh valuation practices concerns. The week saw the alternative asset manager slash the value of its loans to Cary, North Carolina-based specialty materials manufacturer Loparex to near zero.
TPG

was another notable loser with a 10.40% pullback to $47.69. The asset manager faced negative publicity on account of a civil lawsuit filed in Los Angeles against its subsidiary Altus Power by the industrial REIT Lineage over negligence in a fire incident.
Furthermore, TPG was also said to be evaluating the sale of its Lyric business.
Bancorp
was the biggest loser among midcap stocks, falling 25.26% from the previous week to $50.63.
The week saw Chime Financial
agree to acquire the nationally chartered bank and its bank partner for over seven years, Stride, for $590M in cash.

Chime had otherwise been renting the infrastructure model through Stride and Bancorp. As part of the acquisition, Chime stated it intends to consolidate its banking activities under Stride, sending TBBK stock down by about 22.33% the day following Chime's announcement.
FactSet
(-17.01% W/W to $259.71) was another notable decliner. The stock plunged on competition concerns as OpenAI announced the launch of ChatGPT for financial services.
Digital infrastructure solutions provider and cryptocurrency miner Ionic Digital
led the gainers. The stock added 10.60% to $83.39 in a week that saw the company receive provisional ERCOT approval for 466 MW.
Another digital infrastructure platform provider and crypto miner, CleanSpark
followed, adding 8.66% to $13.67.
Stewards
(-21.60% W/W to $2.96), Chaince Digital Holdings
(-19.23% W/W to $2.94), and Teamshares
(+18.63% W/W to $7.36) were among the significant smallcap movers.

title: Blue Owl, FactSet in losers; Wells Fargo, CleanSpark in gainers: week's financials wrap
